requirement:
> `Find regular-expression matches in available files, optionally within a file or directory. Read selected nodes
> separately.`
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.graph.search.search_text.mcp.description` consists of one clause. It is the literal description text for the `search_text` MCP tool: "Find regular-expression matches in available files, optionally within a file or directory. Read selected nodes separately." This constrains what the tool advertises. It doesn't say how the advertisement is built.

No clause prescribes a library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation through a named interface. I considered an alternative implementation. It would define the same string as a constant, or load it from a resource file or a shared definitions table. Every client would still see the same description, so the requirement would still be met. The way the definition is built is therefore discretionary.

The supplied root is `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#impl[Session<'_, D>/ToolSession<D>]/fn[definitions]`. It does emit a `SEARCH_TEXT` definition whose description is exactly that text. That matches the observable output. Because the requirement only specifies observable output, no structural obligation needs implementation evidence. Whether the output is checked is a behavioral-test question, which is outside this review.

behavioral: The requirement has one observable obligation. The `search_text` tool's published description must be exactly: "Find regular-expression matches in available files, optionally within a file or directory. Read selected nodes separately."

`crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[published_tool_descriptions_match_the_contract]` covers it. It builds `ProjectSources`, gets the session definitions, and finds the tool named `search_text`. It then uses `assert_eq!` to compare `tool.description` with the exact required string. An altered, truncated or extended description would fail that assertion. The test carries a `{test}` marker for this requirement.

`search_pages_return_every_original_match_in_order` is also marked for this requirement. It checks the parameter schema and paging, not the description. It adds nothing here, and nothing more is needed.

No other obligations or ambiguities apply.
